known.name: Peri-LN (norm on both sides of each sublayer)
known.mechanism: Applies normalization to the sublayer input and to the sublayer output before the residual add, which bounds the variance each branch contributes to the stream.
known.effect: Reported more balanced variance growth, steadier gradients and better convergence stability than Pre-LN and Post-LN. The search snippets gave no loss numbers.

known.name: LayerNorm Scaling (LNS)
known.mechanism: Multiplies each layer's norm output by 1/sqrt(layer index) so output variance does not grow with depth in Pre-LN.
known.effect: Lower pre-training loss and perplexity than Pre-LN. One version snippet says it reaches Pre-LN's loss with about half the tokens. Combining it with scaled init reduces its benefit, so v3 recommends dropping scaled init.

known.name: OLMo 2 output-norm plus QK-norm
known.mechanism: Moves RMSNorm onto the attention and MLP outputs (h = x + RMSNorm(Attn(x))) and adds QK-norm.
known.effect: Neither change helps alone, but together they improve the growth and spikiness of the gradient L2 norm.

known.name: Mix-LN
known.mechanism: Uses Post-LN in the early layers and Pre-LN in the deeper layers to even out gradient norms across depth.
known.effect: Lowest perplexity at every size tested, for example 18.18 versus 18.65 for Pre-LN at 1B. Post-LN diverged at the larger sizes.
known.where: LLaMA 71M to 1B, plus larger models up to 7B (ICLR 2025)

known.name: HybridNorm
known.mechanism: Normalizes the Q, K and V projections inside attention and uses a different norm placement in the FFN.
known.effect: The HybridNorm* variant had the best average downstream score (60.67). Plain HybridNorm scored 59.18 against 59.56 for Pre-Norm, 59.02 for Post-Norm and 58.83 for Mix-LN.

known.name: Hyper-Connections (static and dynamic)
known.mechanism: Learns the strength of connections between depths across several residual streams. Pre-Norm and Post-Norm are special non-trainable cases.
known.effect: The dynamic variant converged about 1.8x faster on OLMoE and gained 6 points on ARC-Challenge at 500B tokens. Adjacent-layer feature similarity was lower, which the authors read as less representation collapse.

known.name: mHC (manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections)
known.mechanism: Projects the stream-mixing matrices onto the doubly stochastic manifold with Sinkhorn-Knopp to restore the identity-mapping and signal-conservation property.
known.effect: Fixes the instability and scalability limits of unconstrained HC. A secondary blog gives about 1.6x signal amplification against about 3000x for unconstrained HC, at about 6.7% overhead. I did not check these figures against the paper.

known.name: NormFormer extra normalization
known.mechanism: Adds extra norms inside the block (after attention, within the FFN, and per-head scaling) to offset the gradient-magnitude mismatch in Pre-LN.
known.effect: Per its paper, early-layer gradients are much larger than later ones in Pre-LN, and the extra norms address this.

known.name: ReZero / LayerScale (zero or small gated residual branches)
known.mechanism: Gates each residual branch with a zero- or small-initialized scalar or diagonal so each layer starts as the identity.
known.effect: ReZero trains 120-layer Transformers and converges 56% faster on 12-layer enwiki8. LayerScale follows the same motivation, for vision transformers.

known.name: Muon-era speedrun init (zero-initialized projections)
known.mechanism: Initializes output projections and the classifier layer to zero, in a muP-like way.
known.effect: The modded-nanogpt README lists it among the techniques behind the speedup. I found no isolated gain figure.

failed.name: Scaled init combined with LayerNorm Scaling
failed.why: The LNS authors report that scaled initialization combined with LNS reduces LNS's benefit, so they recommend removing scaled init. This is the same interaction as the 1/sqrt(2 n_layer) branch scaling in this recipe.

failed.name: OLMo 2 output-norm or QK-norm used alone
failed.why: The OLMo 2 ablations found that neither change alone gives good results. The benefit comes only from using them together.

failed.name: Plain HybridNorm vs Pre-Norm
failed.why: Plain HybridNorm scored 59.18 on average downstream, below Pre-Norm at 59.56. Only the HybridNorm* variant beat it.

failed.name: Per-layer muP initialization at 10M to 500M parameters
failed.why: In one study, the authors' default initialization beat the per-layer muP variant by 0.68 to 0.92 nats of training loss. muP's optimal learning rate was only more stable across sizes. This is a non-language event-sequence setting and may not transfer to text.

open.direction: Per-stream normalization, or joint normalization over the flattened multi-stream state, compared with normalizing the collapsed read-out
open.why: I found xHC normalizing the flattened multi-stream state, but no ablation of per-stream, joint and collapsed read-out norms in mHC-style models.

open.direction: Depth-dependent norm scaling, such as 1/sqrt(l), combined with stream-mixing weights and no scaled branch init
open.why: LNS shows scaled init and depth-scaled norms interact badly in plain residuals. Nobody has tested this when learned or doubly stochastic mixing weights control the residual.

open.direction: Different init or learning rate for early layers, to equalize the large early-layer gradients, instead of structurally identical layers
open.why: NormFormer documents that early-layer gradients are much larger than later ones in Pre-LN. I found no source testing a per-layer init or learning rate for this.

open.direction: Scaling the input weights of attention and MLP instead of scaling the output (Curse-of-Depth-style fix)
open.why: A non-peer-reviewed blog reports that scaling the input weights beat output scaling, and that pre-softmax attention scores grow unchecked in later layers. This is untested at small scale and in architectures with mixing weights.

open.direction: Fan-in-aware init (muP-style) for compress, expand, rotary and head projections instead of uniform std 0.02
open.why: The Decoder-Hybrid-Decoder paper compares muP, muP++ and standard parameterization (std 0.02 tied, 1e-4 untied embeddings). I found no controlled test at about 21M parameters.
